newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan jails sergeant for sexual harassment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan jails sergeant for sexual harassment.

text.p: An army sergeant has been jailed for sexually harassing male subordinates, a military spokesman said on Tuesday.
The soldier, who was not identified, was sentenced to 3-1/2 years in prison, spokesman Kung Fan-ting said on state-funded television.
The army confirmed the case only after numerous leaks in the popular media and would not give details, though Kung indicated the military was taking sexual harassment seriously.
"We urge (victims) to report similar cases by telephone or through other channels when facing this kind of situation," Kung told reporters.

Sex-related topics -- particularly homosexuality and sexual harassment -- only recently have entered public debate in Taiwan, which has long been dominated by socially conservative Confucian traditions.

Taiwan's social mores have liberalised dramatically since the lifting of martial law in 1987 ended many state strictures on individual behaviour and opened the door to a wide range of liberal foreign influences.
